name: Appsmith Cloud
tagline: Compose an internal dashboard from a database and a fixed widget library

pricing.notes: Typical Business seat rate; verify current cloud packaging.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 5 cloud users; 5 workspaces; 3 Git repositories; unlimited apps

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Up to 99 users; unlimited workspaces, Git repositories, environments and apps
tiers.notes: Cloud bills a user for the full month if that user exists at any point in the month.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Starts at 100 users; unlimited workspaces, Git repositories, environments and apps
tiers.notes: Published starting minimum; managed or air-gapped hosting can cost extra.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 cloud users; 5 workspaces; 3 Git repositories; unlimited apps
pricing.billingTerms: monthly self-serve Business; Enterprise starts at 100 users and is generally contract/annual billed
pricing.hiddenCosts: Business is per user and a user present at any point in a billing month is charged for the whole month; Enterprise has a 100-user/$2,500 monthly floor, while air-gapped, dedicated or managed-hosting services are add-ons

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Appsmith Cloud, compose an internal dashboard from a database and a fixed widget library. The hard boundary is connectors, enterprise permissions, workflows, support, and managed hosting, plus connectors, runtime reliability, and governance.
coreLoopDIY: Define tables and views, compose an internal dashboard from a database and a fixed widget library, connect one approved data source, and deploy it for a small trusted team.
requirements: API credentials for one selected integration
whatYouLose: connectors, enterprise permissions, workflows, support, and managed hosting
ongoingBurden: schema migration, auth, permissions, connector drift, queues, deployments, backups, and auditability
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Appsmith Cloud because the builder is only useful when its runtime, connectors, permissions, and deployments remain boring for years. The recurring cost buys schema migration, auth, permissions, connector drift, queues, deployments, backups, and auditability, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Appsmith
priorArt.desc: Large open-source low-code platform for internal applications and data sources.

alternatives.name: Appsmith Free
alternatives.desc: The same hosted builder is free for five users, five workspaces, public apps, Git, Google sign-in, and standard roles.

facts.install: Hosted signup for Appsmith Cloud Free
facts.engines: Appsmith's AI/agent features use Appsmith-managed AI services; exact model availability is product-controlled rather than a local backend
facts.dataFormat: App definitions, users, and secrets live in Appsmith Cloud; connected business data remains in the source database/API, while query results pass through Appsmith
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same hosted builder with free-tier limits and without the paid plan's advanced roles, audit controls, support, and capacity for a larger production team.

alternatives.name: Budibase
alternatives.desc: Internal apps, forms, automations, and portals in one box; much closer to Knack than its developer branding suggests.

facts.install: Docker image or Docker Compose; Kubernetes is also supported
facts.engines: Model-agnostic; the agent builder supports bring-your-own AI provider credentials
facts.dataFormat: Built-in app data and app definitions are stored in CouchDB, files in MinIO/S3-compatible object storage, and connected external data remains in its source system
facts.gapVsPaid: Budibase's opinionated CRUD components and automations are less flexible than Appsmith's JavaScript-heavy canvas for bespoke dashboards and interactions.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker and persistent storage; production use also means owning upgrades, TLS, backups, and database/network access

alternatives.name: Directus Self-Hosted
alternatives.desc: A polished data studio with tables, forms, dashboards, flows, and APIs; free only below its organization-size ceiling.

facts.install: Docker Compose with SQLite for a test install, or a supported SQL database and persistent file storage for production
facts.engines: Optional AI Assistant supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints with the operator's API key
facts.dataFormat: Business records stay in the connected SQL database; assets live in configured local or object storage; Directus metadata is stored alongside the database
facts.gapVsPaid: Directus provides an excellent database administration studio but not Appsmith's general-purpose widget canvas for composing arbitrary multi-source dashboards.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker, a secret, persistent database/uploads, backups, TLS, and attention to Directus's non-OSI license and free-tier limits

alternatives.name: Lowcoder
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted internal-tool canvas with a broad widget set; less polished, but not a toy.

facts.install: Single Docker image for evaluation, or Docker Compose/Helm with separate MongoDB and Redis services for production
facts.engines: Connectors include OpenAI and other APIs; the operator supplies provider credentials
facts.dataFormat: Users, app definitions, data-source configuration, and assets live in the deployment's MongoDB and mounted lowcoder-stacks volume; Redis holds sessions/state; external business data stays in its source
facts.gapVsPaid: Lowcoder offers a broad canvas but is less polished, less consistently documented, and supported by a smaller connector and community ecosystem than Appsmith Cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker is required; a production deployment needs MongoDB, Redis, secrets, backups, TLS, and more care than the all-in-one demo image

alternatives.name: Retool Free
alternatives.desc: The paid app's real builder, database, mobile apps, and 500 workflow runs for up to five people at $0.

facts.engines: Retool-managed AI models and agents; Free includes pooled AI credits and limited agent hours, while bring-your-own model keys are plan-dependent
facts.dataFormat: App definitions, Retool Database rows, and Retool file storage live in Retool Cloud; connected source data remains in the user's databases/APIs, although query results transit Retool
facts.gapVsPaid: Retool Free is proprietary and capped for a very small team, so it loses Appsmith's open-source escape hatch and paid-team capacity.

alternatives.name: ToolJet Free
alternatives.desc: Two builders, 50 users, two apps, and the actual database and API connectors, not a screenshot-only trial.

facts.install: Hosted signup for ToolJet Cloud Free
facts.engines: ToolJet AI uses vendor-hosted AI services and plan credits; bring-your-own LLM keys are an Enterprise add-on
facts.dataFormat: App metadata, ToolJet Database tables, secrets, and files live in ToolJet Cloud; connected source records remain in their external database/API
facts.gapVsPaid: ToolJet Free's builder and app caps make it a narrower replacement, and its component/debugging experience is less mature than paid Appsmith Cloud.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Business plan and a small-team internal app DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Appsmith Cloud in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: define tables and views, compose an internal dashboard from a database and a fixed widget library, connect one approved data source, and deploy it for a small trusted team.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a schema editor for text, number, boolean, date, enum, and relation fields.
Generate list, detail, create, edit, and kanban views from the schema.
Implement role-based read and write rules for admin and member roles.
Support one REST connector with encrypted credentials and explicit field mapping.
Add an activity log, CSV import or export, backups, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with migrations and a seeded example workspace.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out arbitrary user-authored code execution.
Deliberately leave out a broad integration marketplace.
Deliberately leave out native mobile binaries and enterprise compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
